Anya Patel: Quick sync — Q2 roadmap reprior. Large customer asked to accelerate token-level billing + per-route quotas. Proposing we re-run RICE for three candidates: token billing, adaptive routing v1, and eval-harness automation. Thoughts?

Omar Li: I sketched rough RICE numbers off the top of my head. Token billing looks highest right now but effort may be underestimated. Posting quick table:```
Token billing | R=7 I=6 C=80 E=40 -> 84
Adaptive routing v1 | R=9 I=7 C=70 E=70 -> 63
Eval harness automation | R=5 I=5 C=60 E=20 -> 75
```

Lucy Chen: Good start. We also need to bake in launch criteria for token billing: KMS approved, audit log + pricing docs, SDK bump, and e2e with Dedicated customers. Those add effort risk.

Mike R.: Sequencing point — if we prioritize adaptive routing first we cut infra token cost by ~12% for our median workloads, which reduces the perceived ROI of token billing for some customers. Might make sense to do routing + small billing improvements.

Kevin S.: Heads-up — billing touches legacy metering infra. Effort is at least 60d of eng work + 2 sprints of SRE changes if we want per-route quotas. E=40 is optimistic. If E=60 then token billing score becomes (7*6*80)/60 = 56.

Omar Li: Good catch. Recalc with E=60 -> 56. Eval harness still 75. Adaptive routing still ~63. So order flips: eval harness, adaptive routing, token billing.

Anya Patel: From GTM/customer POV token billing unlocks one large customer's contract this quarter (>$200k ARR), so we should factor that as a binary gating reach bump. Maybe treat that customer as a conditional uplift on Reach.

Lucy Chen: Agreed — for targeted enterprise deals we can project additional churn reduction / revenue influence. But RICE tries to be generic; we can add a separate "strategic/contractual" override if needed.

Mike R.: Also consider parallel work: small-bite token billing (reporting + invoice labels) could be scoped as an MLP (effort 20) to unblock sales, while the full per-route quotas are a follow-up. That splits effort and keeps routing work valuable.

Kevin S.: I like the MLP approach. If we split token billing into "billing reporting (E=20)" and "per-route quotas (E=60)" then billing reporting RICE=(7*5*70)/20 ~ 122 (using conservative 70% confidence), huge. That justifies doing a focused billing MLP.

Anya Patel: OK new proposal: 1) Admit billing-reporting MLP this quarter (owner: Kevin S.), 2) Adaptive routing v1 as second wave (owner: Omar Li), 3) Eval harness automation moves to Q3 unless we can staff a short sprint (owner: Lucy Chen). Can we agree?

prio-bot: Summary created: billing-reporting MLP -> owner Kevin S., adaptive routing v1 -> owner Omar Li, eval-harness -> owner Lucy Chen. Action: 30m re-estimate tomorrow to lock final RICE and launch criteria.

Kevin S.: I'll draft scope for billing-reporting MLP before EOD and tag infra/SRE.

Omar Li: I'll validate routing perf numbers and update effort estimate.

Lucy Chen: I'll prepare acceptance tests for eval harness so we can slot it if capacity frees up.

Anya Patel: Thanks — scheduling 30m sync at 11am PT tomorrow. Please come with updated RICE numbers and any hard blockers. :thumbsup:
